rationale: The candidate is a coherent early massing but it reads as a compact stepped block with limited public threshold intelligence. Across views, the same dominant object is visible, so it is not fragmented, but the silhouette still feels generic and only weakly tied to the neighborhood-living brief. The parcel is roughly contained and the primary road edge is acknowledged, yet the blue access edge does not generate a convincing void, court, or undercut. The form also leans toward a box-plus-cap condition rather than an active ground building with one clear public space and calm upper massing. It is program-plausible at a very coarse level, but not yet a hard pass because the ground/public relation and section logic are underdeveloped.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller tower typology than neighborhood living; transfer the section logic, not the height or tower scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered upper mass can be coherent when paired with a clear dominant body and a legible base.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office tower precedence is not program-equivalent to a compact street building; avoid copying the single-tower typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A strong vertical mass can be paired with a subtle setback/crown to keep hierarchy readable.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a small commercial pavilion; only the active edge/ground relationship is transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple low base with a distinct secondary element can register as an active threshold.

warnings: Primary access edge is not translated into a strong public threshold.
Void/public-space logic is weak relative to the brief.
The stepped top is acceptable as a silhouette move, but it does not yet carry program meaning.
This is not coherent enough as a completed neighborhood-living massing.
No geometry edits proposed because editable_graph_nodes is empty in the supplied graph snapshot.
